problem: Existing image geolocation work (classification, retrieval, and CoT-style LMM reasoning) treats geolocation as a static single-image problem, and existing datasets have no navigable structure, so models cannot actively gather more evidence when cues are missing or ambiguous.
motivation: Humans who are lost move, turn, and approach landmarks to read signs and collect clues. The paper argues that the absence of such active exploration is a bottleneck, and that no open global benchmark supports actions or evaluates a model's ability to propose difficulty-calibrated locations.
key_idea: Replace textual Chain-of-Thought with Action-of-Thought: an LMM iteratively guesses a location, identifies missing evidence, and issues a physical action (rotate or move) in a navigable panorama graph to reduce uncertainty.
insight: Coupling reasoning with actions in a navigable graph gives consistent gains for every tested LMM, with the largest fine-grained gains for strong models (o3 street F1 +0.082) and the largest distance reductions for weak ones (LLaVA-OV-72B -1074 km). Gains at the country level are small because those scales are already saturated. There is no ablation of the action types or the number of steps, so the source of the gains is not isolated.
method: WanderBench construction: 1,047 LMM-proposed locations across six continents at three difficulty levels; each location is a navigable panorama graph (avg 31.27 nodes, 37.67 edges; 32,741 panoramas total) with GPS coordinates and 2048x1024 panoramas.

Location generation: two-stage LMM process. The LMM first describes a region or gives coordinates, then chooses among panorama positions highlighted on a zoom-16 satellite view, requesting extra panoramas until the difficulty level is satisfied.
Graph constraint: every node must be at least 10 steps from any boundary node (degree-1), so the agent can explore 10 steps without backtracking.

Bidirectional evaluation: LMMs are scored both on geolocation (distance, GeoGuessr-style score 100*exp(-10x/18050), and street/city/country accuracy, recall, F1) and on the spatial diversity of the locations they propose (occupancy, entropy, hull area, Clark-Evans ratio, nearest-neighbor distance).

GeoAoT loop: o_t=f_LMM(I_t,h_t); a_t=pi_AoT(o_t); I_{t+1}=T(I_t,a_t). The LMM analyzes cues, identifies missing or ambiguous evidence, proposes an action (e.g. rotate 30° right, move forward 10 m), and updates its guess from the new view.
Training-free deployment: GeoAoT uses structured prompts and pre-trained LMMs with no additional training.

setting.backbone: Off-the-shelf LMMs (frozen): o3, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, Gemma3-27B, InternVL3-78B, LLaVA-OV-72B, Claude Haiku 4.5
setting.observation: equirectangular panoramas / street-view images at graph nodes (RGB), with GPS coordinates and camera poses in the dataset
setting.action_space: discrete navigation-graph actions such as rotate (e.g. 30°) and move forward (e.g. 10 m) along the panorama graph
setting.simulator: other: WanderBench navigable street-view panorama graphs (web-scraped map-service imagery)

numbers_note: WanderBench is a new geolocation benchmark, not a standard navigation benchmark. The paper does not name a split, so 'test' is used. Other w/ AoT rows (LLaVA-OV-72B, Gemma3-27B, InternVL3-78B, Claude Haiku 4.5) are omitted from the numbers. Base-model results are in Table baseline_results (Gemini-2.5 Pro is the best base model at 134.3 km / 95.28).
results: On WanderBench, AoT improves all 7 tested LMMs. o3 goes from 318.8 to 180.3 km and from 92.01 to 94.85 score, and its street accuracy rises from 0.524 to 0.606. Base Gemini-2.5 Pro (134.3 km, 95.28 score) is still better overall than any AoT-augmented model reported, because AoT was not applied to it.
limitations: No ablations of action types, step budget, or comparison with a non-action multi-turn/CoT baseline, so the gain may partly come from extra views or extra inference turns.

Locations and questions are generated by LMMs and imagery is scraped from map services; the dataset may be biased toward model-known locations. Some data details, such as the AoT prompts and Table 1 counts (31K vs 32K), are inconsistent or incomplete.
Gains are small at coarse scales, and AoT was not applied to the best base model (Gemini-2.5 Pro).
